title: Health Experts Warn Viral Mouth Taping Trend Lacks Evidence and May Be Dangerous - NewsBreak
text:
By Fred Peters ,
1 days ago
Published: Sep 25, 2026 - 1:23 p.m.
By Dr. Fred Peters
https://youtube.com/shorts/lNXJqHux5FU?si=d-OJf9S_aV5Kx-To
CLEVELAND, OHIO — Social media feeds are filled with influencers placing strips of tape over their lips before bed to force nasal breathing during the night. It is a trend that has gained millions of views on TikTok. Proponents claim it can do everything from eliminating snoring and boosting oxygen levels to sharpening a person's jawline. While the mechanics of breathing through the nose are backed by biology, experts say the reality of taping the mouth shut is far more complicated than a viral video suggests. Nasal breathing is the body's preferred method for a reason. The nose acts as a natural filtration system that warms and humidifies air before it reaches the lungs. This physiological advantage is well documented, but the leap from nasal breathing being beneficial to mouth taping being a universal cure is not supported by robust data. Research into the practice remains limited. A systematic review of existing literature found only a small number of studies with limited participant groups. While some individuals with mild sleep apnea or specific mouth-breathing habits saw minor improvements, other participants showed no change at all. This lack of broad clinical evidence makes it difficult for medical professionals to recommend the practice to the general public. There are also genuine safety concerns for those with underlying conditions. If someone is mouth breathing because the nasal passages are blocked by a deviated septum, chronic allergies or congestion, removing the secondary airway can be dangerous. It does not solve the root cause of the obstruction; it simply limits the body's ability to get oxygen while the person is unconscious. The more miraculous claims, such as those regarding immune system boosts or structural changes to the jaw, lack any credible scientific backing. The analysis shows that while nasal breathing is verified, taping everyone's mouth shut at night is not. If you are regularly snoring or waking with a dry mouth, do not just tape over the symptom. Schedule an appointment with a primary care physician or a sleep specialist at a local health system to figure out why it is happening.
